summary: The bill requires Medicaid, CHIP, and private health plans to cover one self-measured blood pressure monitoring device per two years for pregnant and postpartum individuals, without cost-sharing or requiring a hypertension diagnosis.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates new coverage under Medicaid (title XIX) and CHIP (title XXI), requiring states to provide self-measured blood pressure monitoring devices to pregnant and postpartum individuals without cost-sharing. This directly increases federal and state expenditures on these public programs, constituting an expansion of government spending on healthcare benefits.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, deductions, credits, or any other tax policy. It only addresses insurance coverage mandates.

The legislation requires coverage of a specific preventive/monitoring service for pregnant and postpartum individuals across Medicaid, CHIP, and all private group/individual health plans (via amendments to PHSA, ERISA, and IRC). It expands mandated benefits and eliminates cost-sharing, pushing the system toward broader required coverage rather than purely market-driven private options.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant eligibility beyond existing Medicaid/CHIP rules.
The bill focuses exclusively on blood pressure monitoring during pregnancy and the postpartum period; it does not address abortion access, funding, or restrictions.
No provisions involve military, defense, or national security spending or policy.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy.

By expanding mandatory Medicaid and CHIP benefits for pregnant and postpartum individuals, the bill enlarges safety-net program coverage for a vulnerable population, directly supporting expanded welfare-style healthcare benefits.
No provisions address schools, education funding, school choice, or workforce training.
No provisions concern drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance use policy.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions involve tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The mandated expansions in Medicaid and CHIP spending increase federal outlays without any offsetting revenue or cuts, thereby contributing to larger deficits rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections, nondiscrimination, or related rights.
No provisions involve foreign assistance, international aid, or State Department programs.
No provisions relate to voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions affect union rights, collective bargaining, or employer-employee relations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.

The bill mandates new Medicaid and CHIP coverage for self-measured blood pressure devices without cost-sharing, directly increasing federal and state outlays with no offsetting revenue or cuts. This effect is a byproduct of the coverage mandate rather than the bill's central purpose.

The bill's entire substance requires government-mandated coverage expansions under Medicaid, CHIP, and private insurance with zero cost-sharing for pregnant and postpartum individuals, representing direct government intervention to expand access and reduce patient costs.
